newsitem.title: USA: Don't resume EEP, U.S. senator urges USDA.
newsitem.headline: Don't resume EEP, U.S. senator urges USDA.

text.p: U.S. Senate Agriculture Committee Chairman Richard Lugar Thursday urged U.S. Agriculture Department resist pressure to renew commodity export subsidies under the Export Enhancement Program (EEP).

In a letter to Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman, Lugar, R- Ind, said renewed EEP would keep world prices artificially low compared with U.S. prices. It would encourage Canada to export wheat to the more lucrative U.S. market, Lugar said.
Renewal of EEP would also harm livestock producers, who were already suffering under high corn prices, the letter, which was dated Sept 17 and released Thursday, said.
"We would be knowingly and deliberately raising livestock producers' operating costs," Lugar said.
Lugar said Glickman would likely come under pressure to resume EEP because of the possibility that the European Union may restart its own commercial wheat export subsidies.
"I urge you to resist the calls for renewed subsidies," the letter said.
